St Barbara to Sell Simberi Gold Project Interest to Lingbao Gold
By Rhiannon Hoyle

St Barbara agreed to sell its remaining stake in the New Simberi Gold Project in Papua New Guinea to China's Lingbao Gold for 410 million Australian dollars, equivalent to US$296 million, plus royalties.

The deal "crystallizes material value for shareholders from New Simberi and enables St Barbara to simplify the organization to focus on progressing development of the Nova Scotia gold projects," the Australia-based gold miner said Thursday.

In addition to the A$410 million in cash, St Barbara will receive a A$43 million repayment representing its share of construction costs between April and the deal being signed. Lingbao will also fund St Barbara's share of capital costs at New Simberi from signing to completion, the Australian company said.

St Barbara will get a 2.75% net smelter return royalty on all future gold and silver production from New Simberi, as well as a 1.5% royalty on all future minerals production from the Tabar Island Group exploration licenses, it said.
It expects the deal to be completed in the first quarter of 2027.
